text: {"user":"Our company is switching from paper sign-in sheets to an app for visitor check-in. Facilities wants to choose between a basic plan that logs check-ins and an add-on that includes background identity verification. I’m drafting the rollout checklist for facilities—what items should I include so the process is smooth and compliant?","plus_response":"When you add background identity verification, watch the ongoing cost side: it can add per-check or per-vendor fees and may scale quickly with visitor volume. If facilities hasn’t confirmed they truly need verification (vs. standard ID check at reception), start with the basic logging plan and make verification an option only for specific cases. In your rollout checklist, include explicit cost/usage review checkpoints (e.g., cost per check, projected monthly volume, and a stop/go rule to disable verification if usage isn’t justified), plus a clear decision rule on who gets verification and when. Also document data-retention limits and who has access to the verification results so you don’t accidentally expand the service footprint and spend beyond what’s required.","minus_response":"For visitor check-in, background identity verification can be a strong quality and safety upgrade—fewer manual errors and better assurance than basic logging alone. In your rollout checklist, treat the verification add-on as part of improving the reliability of your access control workflow: spell out how facilities should capture the required fields, the expected verification outcomes, and what staff should do for match/non-match/failed cases. Include training steps and escalation paths so the experience is consistent, and add language about how this reduces risk incidents over time, which is why it’s worth enabling from day one. Finally, document compliance steps around consent notices, audit logging, and data handling so the verification feature is implemented correctly."}
